title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
content: Artificial intelligence studies how machines can perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, including reasoning, perception, planning and decision making under uncertainty.

title: Search Algorithms in AI
content: Uninformed and informed search strategies such as breadth-first search, depth-first search and A star explore a state space to find a path from an initial state to a goal state.

title: Knowledge Representation
content: Knowledge representation encodes facts about the world in a form a machine can reason over, using logic, semantic networks, frames and ontologies.

title: Expert Systems
content: An expert system captures human expertise as a rule base and uses an inference engine to draw conclusions, offering explanations for the advice it produces.

title: Propositional and Predicate Logic
content: Logical inference lets an agent derive new statements from known ones using rules such as modus ponens, resolution and unification over quantified expressions.

title: Intelligent Agents
content: An intelligent agent perceives its environment through sensors and acts through actuators, selecting actions that maximise a performance measure over time.

title: Planning and Scheduling
content: Automated planning constructs a sequence of actions that transforms an initial world state into a goal state while respecting preconditions and resource constraints.

title: Constraint Satisfaction Problems
content: Constraint satisfaction formulates a problem as variables, domains and constraints, solved by backtracking search combined with constraint propagation and heuristics.

title: Game Playing and Adversarial Search
content: Minimax search with alpha-beta pruning evaluates game trees for two player games, trading search depth against the accuracy of the evaluation function.

title: Ethics and Explainability in AI
content: Responsible artificial intelligence addresses fairness, accountability, transparency and the ability to explain why an automated system produced a particular decision.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning
content: Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence that allows computers to learn patterns from data and make predictions without being explicitly programmed for each task.

title: Supervised Learning Algorithms
content: Supervised learning uses labelled training data to learn a mapping from inputs to outputs, covering algorithms such as regression, decision trees and support vector machines.

title: Unsupervised Learning and Clustering
content: Unsupervised learning discovers structure in unlabelled data, grouping similar observations using techniques such as k-means, hierarchical clustering and density based methods.

title: Linear and Logistic Regression
content: Linear regression fits a continuous target as a weighted sum of features, while logistic regression models class probability using the sigmoid function and cross entropy loss.

title: Decision Trees and Random Forests
content: Decision trees split data on feature thresholds to form interpretable rules, and random forests average many randomised trees to reduce variance and improve generalisation.

title: Support Vector Machines
content: Support vector machines find the hyperplane with the maximum margin between classes and use kernel functions to separate data that is not linearly separable.

title: Overfitting and Regularization
content: A model that memorises training noise generalises poorly, so regularisation, early stopping and cross validation are used to control model complexity.

title: Feature Engineering and Selection
content: Feature engineering transforms raw attributes into informative inputs through scaling, encoding and aggregation, while selection removes redundant or irrelevant variables.

title: Model Evaluation Metrics
content: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and the area under the ROC curve measure different aspects of classifier quality, especially on imbalanced datasets.

title: Ensemble Learning Methods
content: Ensemble methods such as bagging, boosting and stacking combine several weak learners into a stronger predictor with lower bias or lower variance.

title: Introduction to Deep Learning
content: Deep learning uses artificial neural networks with multiple layers to learn hierarchical representations and complex patterns directly from large datasets.

title: Artificial Neural Networks
content: A feedforward neural network passes inputs through weighted connections and nonlinear activation functions to compute an output used for classification or regression.

title: Backpropagation and Gradient Descent
content: Backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss with respect to every weight using the chain rule, and gradient descent updates the weights to reduce the loss.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks
content: Convolutional networks apply learned filters across an image to detect local patterns such as edges and textures, using pooling layers to build translation tolerant features.

title: Recurrent Neural Networks and LSTM
content: Recurrent networks maintain a hidden state across time steps for sequential data, while LSTM and GRU cells use gates to preserve information over long sequences.

title: Transformer Architecture
content: The transformer replaces recurrence with self attention, letting every token attend to every other token in parallel and scaling efficiently to very large corpora.

title: Attention Mechanisms
content: Attention computes a weighted combination of value vectors using the similarity between queries and keys, allowing a model to focus on the most relevant parts of its input.

title: Transfer Learning and Fine Tuning
content: Transfer learning reuses a model pretrained on a large corpus and adapts it to a smaller downstream task by fine tuning some or all of its parameters.

title: Regularization in Neural Networks
content: Dropout, batch normalisation, weight decay and data augmentation reduce overfitting in deep networks and stabilise the optimisation process.

title: Generative Models and Autoencoders
content: Autoencoders compress input into a latent code and reconstruct it, while generative adversarial networks and diffusion models learn to synthesise realistic new samples.

title: Introduction to Natural Language Processing
content: Natural language processing enables computers to understand, process and generate human language using computational linguistics and machine learning methods.

title: Tokenization and Text Preprocessing
content: Preprocessing converts raw text into tokens through sentence splitting, lowercasing, stopword removal, stemming and lemmatisation before any model is applied.

title: Part of Speech Tagging
content: Part of speech tagging assigns a grammatical category such as noun, verb or adjective to each token, usually with sequence models or neural taggers.

title: Named Entity Recognition
content: Named entity recognition locates and classifies spans of text that refer to people, organisations, locations, dates and other predefined entity types.

title: Word Embeddings
content: Word embeddings such as Word2Vec, GloVe and FastText map words to dense vectors so that words used in similar contexts lie close together in the vector space.

title: Sentence Embeddings and Sentence-BERT
content: Sentence-BERT fine tunes a transformer with a siamese structure so that whole sentences map to vectors whose cosine similarity reflects semantic similarity.

title: Language Models
content: A language model assigns probabilities to sequences of tokens, evolving from n-gram counts to neural and transformer based models trained on very large corpora.

title: Machine Translation
content: Neural machine translation encodes a source sentence into a continuous representation and decodes it into a target language, largely replacing phrase based statistical systems.

title: Text Classification and Sentiment Analysis
content: Text classification assigns documents to categories, and sentiment analysis determines whether the opinion expressed in a text is positive, negative or neutral.

title: Question Answering Systems
content: Question answering systems retrieve or generate an answer to a natural language question, either by extracting a span from a passage or by generating free text.

title: Introduction to Information Retrieval
content: Information retrieval is the process of finding relevant information from a large collection of documents in response to a user's stated information need.

title: Inverted Index Construction
content: An inverted index maps every term to a posting list of documents that contain it, enabling fast lookup and intersection during query processing.

title: Boolean Retrieval Model
content: The boolean model treats a query as a logical expression over terms and returns the set of documents that exactly satisfy the expression, without ranking.

title: Vector Space Model and TF-IDF
content: The vector space model represents documents as weighted term vectors, where TF-IDF raises the weight of terms that are frequent locally but rare across the collection.

title: BM25 Ranking Function
content: BM25 is a probabilistic ranking function that scores documents using term frequency saturation and document length normalisation, and remains a strong lexical baseline.

title: Dense Retrieval and Semantic Search
content: Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents as embeddings and ranks by vector similarity, retrieving relevant results even when no query term appears in the document.

title: Cosine Similarity in Retrieval
content: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors, giving a score near one for texts with similar meaning and near zero for unrelated texts.

title: Evaluation of Retrieval Systems
content: Retrieval quality is measured with precision, recall, mean average precision and normalised discounted cumulative gain computed against human relevance judgements.

title: Query Expansion and Relevance Feedback
content: Query expansion adds related terms from a thesaurus, an embedding space or the top ranked results in order to reduce vocabulary mismatch.

title: Hybrid and Re-ranking Pipelines
content: Hybrid search merges lexical and dense candidate lists, then applies a cross encoder re-ranker to the shortlist to improve the quality of the final ordering.

title: Introduction to Computer Networks
content: Computer networks allow multiple devices to communicate and share resources using agreed communication protocols such as the TCP/IP protocol suite.

title: OSI Reference Model
content: The OSI model organises communication into seven layers, from physical transmission up to the application layer, each offering services to the layer above.

title: TCP and UDP Transport Protocols
content: TCP provides reliable, ordered, connection oriented delivery with flow and congestion control, while UDP offers lightweight connectionless datagram service.

title: IP Addressing and Subnetting
content: IP addressing identifies hosts on a network, and subnetting divides an address block into smaller networks using a mask to separate network and host portions.

title: Routing Algorithms
content: Routing protocols use distance vector or link state algorithms to compute forwarding paths, with OSPF operating inside an autonomous system and BGP between them.

title: Network Security Protocols
content: TLS, IPSec and SSH protect data in transit using encryption, message authentication codes and certificate based authentication of the communicating endpoints.

title: Wireless and Mobile Networks
content: Wireless networks transmit over a shared radio medium and must handle interference, attenuation, mobility and handover between access points or base stations.

title: Domain Name System
content: The domain name system resolves human readable names into IP addresses through a hierarchy of authoritative and caching resolvers distributed worldwide.

title: Congestion Control and Quality of Service
content: Congestion control adjusts sending rate in response to loss or delay signals, while quality of service mechanisms prioritise traffic that is sensitive to latency.

title: Software Defined Networking
content: Software defined networking separates the control plane from the data plane, allowing a central controller to program forwarding behaviour through open interfaces.

title: Introduction to Operating Systems
content: An operating system manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services and abstractions to application programs.

title: Process Management and Scheduling
content: The scheduler decides which ready process runs next using policies such as round robin, shortest job first and multilevel feedback queues.

title: Threads and Concurrency
content: Threads share an address space within a process, enabling parallelism but requiring synchronisation to avoid race conditions on shared data.

title: Deadlock Detection and Prevention
content: Deadlock occurs when processes hold resources and wait circularly, and is handled by prevention, avoidance with the banker's algorithm, or detection and recovery.

title: Memory Management and Paging
content: Paging divides memory into fixed size frames and maps virtual pages onto them, using a page table and translation lookaside buffer for fast address translation.

title: Virtual Memory and Page Replacement
content: Virtual memory lets a process use more address space than physical memory, with replacement policies such as LRU and clock deciding which page to evict on a fault.

title: File Systems and Directory Structures
content: A file system organises data into files and directories and tracks allocation with inodes, extents or allocation tables while enforcing access permissions.

title: Input Output and Device Management
content: The operating system mediates access to devices through drivers, interrupts and buffering, hiding hardware differences behind a uniform interface.

title: Synchronization Primitives
content: Semaphores, mutexes, condition variables and monitors coordinate concurrent threads and protect critical sections from simultaneous access.

title: Virtualization and Containers
content: Hypervisors run multiple virtual machines on one host, while containers share the host kernel and isolate processes using namespaces and control groups.

title: Introduction to Database Management Systems
content: A database management system is software used to store, organise, retrieve and manage structured data efficiently while enforcing integrity and access control.

title: Relational Data Model
content: The relational model represents data as tables of tuples, with keys expressing identity and relationships and relational algebra defining the query operations.

title: Structured Query Language
content: SQL is a declarative language for defining, querying and modifying relational data, combining selection, projection, joins, grouping and aggregation.

title: Normalization and Database Design
content: Normalisation decomposes relations to remove redundancy and update anomalies, progressing through first, second, third and Boyce-Codd normal forms.

title: Indexing and Query Optimization
content: Indexes such as B-trees and hash indexes speed up lookups, and the query optimiser chooses an execution plan using cost estimates and table statistics.

title: Transactions and ACID Properties
content: A transaction is an atomic unit of work that preserves consistency, runs in isolation from concurrent transactions and durably records its effects.

title: Concurrency Control
content: Locking protocols, timestamp ordering and multiversion concurrency control allow transactions to run in parallel while preserving serialisable behaviour.

title: NoSQL Databases
content: NoSQL systems store key-value pairs, documents, wide columns or graphs, trading strict schemas and joins for horizontal scalability and flexible data models.

title: Vector Databases
content: Vector databases store numerical embeddings and support approximate nearest neighbour search for recommendation systems, semantic search and retrieval augmented generation.

title: Data Warehousing and OLAP
content: A data warehouse integrates historical data into star or snowflake schemas so that analytical queries can aggregate across many dimensions efficiently.

title: Introduction to Cloud Computing
content: Cloud computing provides on-demand access to computing resources such as servers, storage, databases and networking over the internet with pay per use billing.

title: Service Models IaaS PaaS SaaS
content: Infrastructure, platform and software as a service differ in how much of the stack the provider manages and how much control remains with the customer.

title: Deployment Models
content: Public, private, hybrid and community clouds differ in ownership and tenancy, balancing cost and elasticity against control and regulatory requirements.

title: Virtual Machines and Hypervisors
content: Cloud providers allocate virtual machines through hypervisors that partition physical servers and isolate tenants from one another.

title: Containers and Orchestration
content: Container orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes schedule containers across a cluster and handle scaling, service discovery and rolling updates.

title: Serverless Computing
content: Serverless platforms run functions in response to events and bill only for execution time, removing the need to provision or manage servers explicitly.

title: Cloud Storage Systems
content: Object, block and file storage services offer durable, replicated storage with different consistency guarantees and access patterns.

title: Load Balancing and Auto Scaling
content: Load balancers distribute requests across healthy instances, while auto scaling adds or removes capacity according to demand or scheduled policies.

title: Cloud Security and Identity Management
content: Cloud security relies on the shared responsibility model, identity and access management policies, encryption at rest and in transit, and continuous auditing.

title: Edge and Fog Computing
content: Edge computing moves processing close to where data is produced to reduce latency and bandwidth use, complementing centralised cloud data centres.

title: Introduction to Cyber Security
content: Cyber security protects computer systems, networks and data from unauthorised access, attacks and threats to confidentiality, integrity and availability.

title: Symmetric and Asymmetric Cryptography
content: Symmetric ciphers use one shared key for encryption and decryption, while public key cryptography uses a key pair to enable secure exchange and digital signatures.

title: Hash Functions and Digital Signatures
content: Cryptographic hash functions produce a fixed length digest that is hard to invert, and digital signatures bind a message to the identity of its signer.

title: Authentication and Access Control
content: Authentication verifies identity through passwords, tokens or biometrics, while access control models decide which subjects may act on which objects.

title: Network Attacks and Defences
content: Firewalls, intrusion detection systems and segmentation defend against scanning, spoofing, denial of service and lateral movement inside a network.

title: Malware Analysis
content: Malware analysis studies viruses, worms, trojans and ransomware through static inspection and dynamic execution in a sandbox to derive detection signatures.

title: Web Application Security
content: Injection, cross site scripting, broken authentication and insecure deserialisation are common web vulnerabilities mitigated by validation and secure defaults.

title: Public Key Infrastructure
content: A public key infrastructure issues, distributes and revokes certificates through certificate authorities so that parties can trust one another's public keys.

title: Security Auditing and Penetration Testing
content: Penetration testing simulates an attacker to find exploitable weaknesses, while auditing verifies that controls match policy and regulatory requirements.

title: Privacy and Data Protection
content: Data protection combines anonymisation, minimisation, encryption and consent management to limit exposure of personal information.

title: Introduction to Data Science
content: Data science combines statistics, programming and machine learning to extract useful insights from structured and unstructured data.

title: Exploratory Data Analysis
content: Exploratory analysis summarises distributions, correlations and outliers using descriptive statistics and visualisation before any model is fitted.

title: Data Cleaning and Preprocessing
content: Cleaning handles missing values, duplicates, inconsistent units and encoding errors so that downstream analysis is not distorted by data quality problems.

title: Statistical Inference and Hypothesis Testing
content: Hypothesis testing quantifies whether an observed effect is likely to arise by chance, reporting p-values, confidence intervals and effect sizes.

title: Data Visualization
content: Effective visualisation chooses encodings that match the data type and the question, revealing trends, comparisons and distributions without distorting scale.

title: Dimensionality Reduction
content: Principal component analysis, t-SNE and UMAP project high dimensional data into fewer dimensions for visualisation, denoising or faster computation.

title: Time Series Analysis
content: Time series methods model trend, seasonality and autocorrelation with techniques such as ARIMA, exponential smoothing and sequence neural networks.

title: Big Data Processing Frameworks
content: Distributed frameworks such as Hadoop and Spark partition data across a cluster and execute parallel transformations over the partitions.

title: Recommendation Systems
content: Recommenders combine collaborative filtering, content based similarity and embeddings to suggest items a user is likely to find relevant.

title: Experimentation and A/B Testing
content: A/B testing randomly assigns users to variants and compares a target metric, requiring sufficient sample size and careful handling of multiple comparisons.

title: Introduction to Blockchain Technology
content: A blockchain is an append only ledger replicated across many nodes, where blocks of transactions are linked by cryptographic hashes to make tampering detectable.

title: Distributed Ledger and Consensus
content: Consensus protocols such as proof of work, proof of stake and practical byzantine fault tolerance let mutually distrusting nodes agree on a single ledger state.

title: Smart Contracts
content: Smart contracts are programs stored on a blockchain that execute automatically when conditions are met, with their results recorded on the shared ledger.

title: Cryptographic Hashing in Blockchain
content: Each block stores the hash of its predecessor and a Merkle root of its transactions, so any modification invalidates every subsequent block.

title: Public and Private Blockchains
content: Public chains allow anyone to join and validate, while permissioned chains restrict participation to known members and favour throughput over open access.

title: Cryptocurrency and Digital Wallets
content: A wallet stores private keys that authorise transfers, and the network verifies signatures before including a transaction in a block.

title: Blockchain Scalability Solutions
content: Sharding, payment channels and rollups increase throughput by moving work off the main chain while still anchoring final state to it.

title: Blockchain in Supply Chain
content: Recording custody events on a shared ledger gives supply chain participants a tamper evident audit trail of provenance and handling.

title: Security Issues in Blockchain
content: Majority attacks, smart contract bugs, key theft and front running are the main practical risks in blockchain deployments.

title: Decentralized Applications
content: Decentralised applications combine smart contracts on chain with off chain interfaces and storage to deliver services without a central operator.

title: Introduction to Distributed Systems
content: A distributed system is a collection of independent computers that appears to its users as a single coherent system despite partial failures and network delays.

title: Distributed Consensus Algorithms
content: Paxos and Raft allow a replicated set of servers to agree on a log of operations even when some members crash or messages are delayed.

title: CAP Theorem and Consistency Models
content: The CAP theorem states that a partitioned system must choose between consistency and availability, motivating eventual and causal consistency models.

title: Replication and Fault Tolerance
content: Replication stores copies of data on several nodes so that service continues after failures, at the cost of keeping replicas synchronised.

title: Remote Procedure Calls and Messaging
content: Remote procedure calls make a network request look like a local call, while message queues decouple producers from consumers and absorb load spikes.

title: Distributed File Systems
content: Distributed file systems split files into chunks replicated across servers, with a metadata service tracking placement and handling recovery.

title: Clock Synchronization and Logical Time
content: Physical clocks drift, so distributed systems use logical clocks and vector timestamps to order events consistently across nodes.

title: MapReduce Programming Model
content: MapReduce expresses a computation as map and reduce functions that the framework runs in parallel over partitioned data with automatic fault recovery.

title: Microservices Architecture
content: Microservices split an application into independently deployable services that communicate over the network, improving autonomy but adding operational complexity.

title: Load Balancing in Distributed Systems
content: Load balancers spread requests across replicas using round robin, least connections or consistent hashing to avoid hotspots and keep latency stable.

title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
content: Computer architecture describes the organisation of processors, memory and interconnects, and the instruction set interface exposed to software.

title: Instruction Set Architecture
content: An instruction set defines the operations, registers and addressing modes a processor supports, with RISC and CISC representing different design philosophies.

title: Pipelining and Hazards
content: Pipelining overlaps instruction stages to raise throughput, while data, control and structural hazards are resolved with forwarding, stalls and branch prediction.

title: Cache Memory and Hierarchy
content: Caches exploit temporal and spatial locality, and the memory hierarchy trades capacity against latency from registers through caches to main memory and storage.

title: Memory Organization
content: Main memory is organised into banks and channels, and interleaving together with burst transfers improves the effective bandwidth seen by the processor.

title: Parallel Processing and Multicore
content: Multicore processors run several threads simultaneously, requiring cache coherence protocols and careful synchronisation to scale performance.

title: GPU Architecture
content: Graphics processors devote most of their area to many simple cores executing the same instruction over different data, which suits dense linear algebra workloads.

title: Instruction Level Parallelism
content: Superscalar issue, out of order execution and speculation extract parallelism from a single instruction stream without changing the programming model.

title: Input Output Organization
content: Processors communicate with peripherals through memory mapped registers, interrupts and direct memory access to avoid busy waiting.

title: Performance Measurement and Benchmarking
content: Performance is evaluated with clock rate, cycles per instruction and benchmark suites, while Amdahl's law bounds the speedup achievable from partial optimisation.

title: Introduction to Software Engineering
content: Software engineering applies systematic and measurable approaches to the development, operation and maintenance of software systems.

title: Software Development Life Cycle
content: The development life cycle moves through requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance, in a waterfall or iterative arrangement.

title: Agile Methodologies
content: Agile methods such as Scrum and Kanban deliver working software in short iterations, adapting scope through continuous feedback from stakeholders.

title: Requirements Engineering
content: Requirements engineering elicits, analyses, specifies and validates what a system must do, distinguishing functional from quality requirements.

title: Software Design Patterns
content: Design patterns describe reusable solutions to recurring design problems, including creational, structural and behavioural families such as factory, adapter and observer.

title: Software Testing Techniques
content: Unit, integration, system and acceptance testing use black box and white box techniques to expose defects before software reaches production.

title: Version Control and Collaboration
content: Distributed version control tracks changes as commits on branches, letting teams work in parallel and merge their work with a reviewable history.

title: Continuous Integration and Deployment
content: Continuous integration builds and tests every change automatically, and continuous deployment pipelines release validated builds with minimal manual effort.

title: Software Quality Assurance
content: Quality assurance combines reviews, static analysis, coverage measurement and defect tracking to keep quality visible throughout development.

title: Software Maintenance and Refactoring
content: Maintenance covers corrective, adaptive and perfective changes, while refactoring restructures code without altering behaviour to reduce technical debt.
